A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETNN research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–K are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v4 reports original ETNN experiments on QM9, air-pollution downscaling, and synthetic graph distinguishability, alongside ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and reports revised air-pollution results averaged over 30 seeds.

M1.justification: The ETNN feature and position updates, geometric invariants, architecture, and lifting configurations are retained. Equation (13) corrects a duplicated containment condition to match the neighborhood already described in v4; this does not establish a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate QM9 molecular properties, the same Bronx air-pollution dataset, 4-chain graphs, and scalarization counterexamples. No dataset, population, task, or evaluated input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the molecular, air-pollution, synthetic, and computational comparisons. Removing the asterisk from DimeNet++ in Table 1 changes its label, not the comparator or scores. The new EMPSN discussion in Appendix F introduces no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes air-pollution reporting from RMSE to average R², R² differences for ablations, and MSE. The documented splits, training budgets, and model settings remain unchanged. Appendix I.2.3 still specifies RMSE, leaving the metric documentation inconsistent. Newly disclosed Mercator projection does not establish a preprocessing change.

E4.justification: Table 2b revises the evidence for removing the virtual cell, position updates, and geometric features: it now provides absolute MSE and R² differences with uncertainty instead of a single percentage-change column. No ablation variant is added; the QM9 and synthetic expressiveness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: For the air-pollution experiment, Section 5 explicitly changes the reported averaging count from 3 to 30 seeds. Table 2 adds standard errors for baseline and ablation R² results, with the standard-error formula stated in the text. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting for a principal application.

E6.justification: Air-pollution results are replaced: ETNN has RMSE 0.939 in v4, versus MSE 0.935 and average R² 9.34% in v5. Different metrics and seed counts prevent interpreting this as a direct performance gain. ETNN remains best, while GNN replaces MLP as the strongest other baseline. Ablation values change; Tables 1, 3–6, 11, and 12 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: v5 corrects Equation (13) to require both cells to belong to the maximal-rank cell and corrects the geospatial representation's codomain from T to P(T). Appendix F adds an explicit corollary specifying a condition for strict expressivity advantage. Proposition 3 formalizes the disconnected Lift 3a failure already explained in v4, rather than introducing a new counterexample.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and conclusion retain the same claims about a unifying equivariant framework, expressivity, molecular and geospatial applications, and computational advantages. Added wording emphasizes the existing inductive-bias argument without changing the claimed contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds a rationale connecting Mercator coordinates, distance information, and Euclidean equivariance. Appendix F's new Remark 7 explains an expressivity advantage over skeleton-preserving simplicial lifts through the absence of triangles or cliques. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged; the existing disconnected-lift limitation becomes more prominent.

D1.justification: v5 newly specifies Mercator-projected coordinates for the geospatial experiment and adds Appendix I.3 summarizing coordinate features and their inheritance by higher ranks. Architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access information are retained. The repository URL is merely relocated and written explicitly.

R1.justification: v5 adds Ayers (1992) for geospatial representations, Li et al. (2024a) for path-complex molecular networks, and Eitan et al. (2024) for CCMPN expressivity. Related-work discussion expands modestly, and Appendix F adds a comparison with EMPSN expressivity; the overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Changes include the ICLR publication header, a localized rewrite of geospatial-complex definitions, additional explanatory paragraphs, and the new geometric-features subsection. The overall section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 is widened and reorganized around R², standard-error, and MSE columns. Table 1 adds best-score highlighting. Existing appendix tables and figures shift with pagination, but all figure images are unchanged; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The clearest gain is more assessable air-pollution evidence: v4's three-seed point estimates become 30-seed results with standard errors. Corrected definitions and coordinate disclosures also improve clarity. Gains remain limited because the main method and other empirical results are unchanged, Appendix I.2.3 still describes RMSE, and the reported ablation effects are smaller than their standard errors, limiting strong component-effect conclusions.
